And yet by 4.38pm local time – nine hours after Pat Cummins had finished his marathon takedown of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography in Sydney – Harry Brook’s side were 1-0 down once again. Rolled for 131 all out in just 33.4 overs, having been 68 for eight at one stage, a seven-wicket loss was the upshot. articles.description: Australian cricket captain breaks silence over allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about 2018 ball tampering in South Africa After a torrid week, Australia’s Test captain, Pat Cummins, promised he would answer every question thrown at him in one of the most eagerly anticipated press conferences in recent sporting memory. articles.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
articles.description: The Ballon d’Or validated the forward’s career and he extended his incredible record for England with yet another goal on his 126th appearance Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we? This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue. articles.title: Chess: Carlsen comes to town with tantalising tests for London Classic Super Rapid
articles.description: The Norwegian world No 1 will be among 500 competitors in the 10-round contest of 15-minute games Magnus Carlsen makes a very rare appearance in an open tournament on 5-6 December when the Norwegian, who has topped the world rankings for 15 successive years, competes in the 10-round Super Rapid at the XTX Markets London Classic. The venue is the Novotel West at Hammersmith and the time limit is 15 minutes per player for the entire game, plus a 10 seconds increment for each move. In 2025, 267 players entered the Super Rapid. Well, at least the idea of Nashville, the country music mecca that is perpetually struggling to define itself within and against the country at large, a place that has always been more diverse than its reputation yet still stands for a certain image of white, Christian Americana. There are plenty of enduring contradictions to mine there – the hyper-masculine men singing with their hearts on their sleeve, the Madonna-badass complex among its relatively few female stars, the suburban money in a genre ostensibly speaking to the rural common man. Netflix seems to be aiming for some of those complexities with Heartland, a patchy neo-noir thriller starring Jessica Chastain as a washed-up former star turned vigilante detective with an axe to grind on Music Row. articles.title: Sheherazaad: Khudgarzi review | Ammar Kalia's global album of the month
articles.description: (Erased Tapes) Dreamy, reverb-laden arrangements, virtuosic vocals and echoes of PJ Harvey and Massive Attack make this disarming debut a one-of-a-kind creation Since the release of her debut EP, Qasr , in 2024, south Asian-American vocalist and composer Sheherazaad has developed a distinctive take on the classical singing of her heritage. While her contemporaries such as the singers Ganavya and Manizeh draw on spiritual vocal traditions, and Arooj Aftab on jazz and folk instrumentation, Sheherazaad’s work is darker and far more introspective, using sparse acoustic arrangements to create a style of Urdu-language noir. On this debut album, she delivers her most disarmingly eerie and mournful work yet. A heavy layer of reverb coats the record’s spare and often evocative arrangements, making undulating tabla hits echo beneath Sheherazaad’s keening vocals on Qatil, while on Registaan it lends an unnervingly distorted quality to a simple guitar refrain and on Mard it subsumes melody in a haze of resonance. The resulting atmosphere sits somewhere between PJ Harvey’s late-90s eerie grunge and the trip-hop qawwali of Massive Attack’s work with singer Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan – an ambience tha

articles.title: Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love review – raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats
articles.description: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. Aalegra’s fourth album is her most successful front-to-back statement yet, even if she can’t shake off the talent-show-ish reverence for her idols. articles.description: From the Isle of Skye to the Cairngorms, our explorers find white-sand beaches, secret lochs and solitude • Tell us about your favourite European national park – the best tip wins a £200 holiday voucher At Camasunary bay on the Strathaird peninsula of the Isle of Skye, we watched an otter at low tide lifting seaweed to find crabs. Boots off, we crossed one of Skye’s shortest (and coldest) rivers, before slogging upwards through unforgiving heather to the col beneath the pathless hill Sgùrr na Strì . The mountain view from the summit’s glaciated slabs is perhaps the finest in Scotland – or even Europe. Below is landlocked Loch Coruisk, girdled by the black teeth of the entire Cuillin ridge. articles.title: NI Water Works - Cornagrade Road Enniskillen 3 Aug
articles.description: Essential Water Infrastructure Improvement Work gets underway – Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen NI Water is set to commence an upgrade of the water infrastructure on Cornagrade Road, Enniskillen in early August for approximately 6 weeks. The work will see around 400m of new watermain being laid along Cornagrade Road, starting at Cherrymount Roundabout on Monday 3 rd August and progressing as far as the second entrance to Kilmacormick Road. To facilitate the laying of this new watermain, a lane closure will be in place around each working area and signage will be in place. Working areas will be kept as short as possible (around 100m) with temporary traffic lights in place to manage the flow of traffic. Access to residential and business properties on and adjacent to Cornagrade Road will be available at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be affected for a short period of time while the pipelaying passes. Any bus stop located within a working area will be temporarily relocated.

articles.title: Derry - NIW Scheme - Racecourse Rd - from 27 July
articles.description: Essential water network upgrade to get underway on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett NI Water is set to begin an essential watermain upgrade on Racecourse Road, Ballyarnett (Derry/Londonderry) on Monday 27 th July to improve the resilience of the local water supply network. The work, which involves laying around 170 metres of new watermain between Carnhill Roundabout and Greenhaw Road, will replace a section of the 50-year-old Ballyarnett Water Trunkmain which has been prone to bursts. The upgrade will help to protect homes from flooding, should a burst occur in the future, and provide improved access for NI Water maintenance. A l ane closure controlled by temporary traffic lights will be in place on Racecourse Road around the working area from Monday 27 th July for four weeks. A further two weeks of work will take place in the adjacent verge which will not require any traffic management. Temporary traffic lights will be manned during peak hours and access to properties will be maintained at all times, although parking spaces within the working area will be temporarily unavailable. Once the lane closure is removed, works will move into the adjacent verge to complete the final phase of w

articles.title: Craigavon - Closure of Maple Path & Parkmore Footbridges
articles.description: Closure of Maple Path and Parkmore Footbridges, Craigavon The Department for Infrastructure have announced that the Maple Path and Parkmore footbridges in Craigavon will be closed from Thursday 4 June 2026. Detailed engineering inspections identified structural concerns, and it has been concluded that the closure of these footbridges is necessary while a permanent solution is developed. Alternative local walking routes are available and will be signposted where appropriate. While these routes may increase journey times for some users, they will provide access around the affected areas. The Department recognises the importance of both footbridges to local residents and apologises for any inconvenience caused. However, as the Department’s infrastructure assets age there will always be an eventual need to replace structures that present safety issues or have come to the end of their natural lifespan. Further information on future proposals for the bridges will be provided as work progresses. The Department would like to thank the public for their patience and cooperation.

articles.title: Transcription by Ben Lerner audiobook review – a mediation on memory for the smartphone era
articles.description: Actor Seth Numrich vividly captures the neurotic tendencies of a middle-aged man with a digital dependency, in an intense multilayered tale of family and storytelling We meet the unnamed narrator of Transcription on a train to Providence, Rhode Island. He is going to interview his one-time mentor Thomas, a celebrated German writer and film-maker, who is 90 and who, owing to his age, probably won’t be interviewed again. The narrator confesses to his young daughter, Eva, that he is nervous about the meeting. Those nerves are replaced by panic when he gets to his hotel and drops his iPhone into a sink of water, rendering it useless. Not only does he have no means of recording the interview, he won’t be able to FaceTime Eva at bedtime. Ben Lerner’s novella is a thoughtful meditation on memory, storytelling and lives lived through technology. The middle-aged narrator’s anxiety over his phone falls away as he engages with the world around him and with his past. articles.title: Second world war ‘brain’ bunker in cliffs of Dover opens to public
articles.description: Hidden bunker, entered via a hatch in a field, controlled a gun battery used to attack German ships in Channel It has been kept secret for decades, buried four metres deep into the white cliffs of Dover. But from Friday, members of the public will finally be able to visit a pioneering command bunker that was ordered by Winston Churchill and proved a vital defence during the second world war. The Fan Bay plotting room , which is encased in concrete, housed the first land-based computer-aided targeting system. This acted as a “brain” for a gun battery that was used to defend Dover and attack German ships in the Channel, according to Jon Barker, who led the excavation project for the National Trust. The findings prompted private congressional and White House inquiries into workforce conditions and mental healthcare. The deaths involved military personnel, civilians, and contractors. Ten occurred near Fort Meade, Maryland , and one near an NSA facility in Georgia. Five deaths between early June and early July formed a cluster that Bloomberg previously reported . Officials have not established a single explanation for the losses. "The pace of operations right now at both NSA and Cyber Command can be overwhelming," former intelligence executive Harry Coker Jr. told Bloomberg. "There is a lot of stress that a lot of us overlook because we think cyber is away from the front , and physically that's accurate but intellectually and emotionally it's inaccurate." articles.description: Mamdani Hands Nonprofits First Crack At Buying Troubled NYC Apartment Buildings Authored by AG News Staff via American Greatness , New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has signed a law giving nonprofits and community groups the first chance to buy certain apartment buildings before they reach the private market. Mamdani signed the Community Opportunity to Purchase Act, known as COPA, on Tuesday. When a covered building goes up for sale, those groups will get an "exclusive 145-day window to complete the purchase." Even if an owner rejects the group's offer, the law gives the group a right of first refusal. If another buyer makes an offer within the following year, the qualified entity can match it. articles.title: ‘My partners would all tell you I was a nut job’: Jane Wiedlin on the Go-Go’s, fame and the freedom of sex dungeons
articles.description: As she releases a brutally honest memoir, the new wave icon opens up about industry sexism, living with bipolar disorder and becoming ‘the world’s first atheist ordained minister’ The first thing Jane Wiedlin tells me before our interview even begins is that, an hour or so earlier, she downed two beers. “It keeps me cheerful,” she says with a laugh. The disclosure dovetails with the reason we’re doing the interview in the first place, which is to unpack her new memoir, a tome that deserves a truth-in-advertising award for its title alone: TMI (as in “too much information”). “I’ve always been TMI!” Wiedlin proudly announces. “I’m the one who always wanted to expose the truth. This book is my first opportunity to do so.” A portion of that truth has to do with the band she helped form in the late 70s, the Go-Go’s. The five-piece are not only the first all-female band who play their own instruments and write their own material to earn a No 1 album in the US but, astonishingly, are the only such group to hold that distinction nearly 45 years later. The group’s power-pop music, heard in zippy hits like Our Lips Are Sealed and Vacation, led to their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall o

articles.title: Ten Lives by Mona Chalabi review – what if we were totally honest about our wealth?
articles.description: The data journalist puts her own finances – and those of 10 others from across the economic spectrum – under a microscope How much do you earn? If the question makes you bristle – and I realise we haven’t even met – would you answer it if someone convinced you that your candour might just change the world? In her deliciously original first book, the former Guardian data journalist and illustrator Mona Chalabi sets out to do precisely that. The result – a dazzling mix of journalism, data visualisation and memoir – is both a joy to read and a serious provocation. Chalabi takes aim at our silence and furtiveness around individual income and finances. “Our collective ignorance is sustaining an unfair system,” she argues. Unless we talk more openly about our personal wealth, we will never be able to tackle the economic problems causing insecurity and anxiety for us all. Continue reading...

Then the fashion house came calling Before Paris, there was Lagos, with its busy markets, roadside stalls and maze of disorderly streets. And then there was Rachel Ojuromi, sashaying through it all and turning the everyday into an unlikely catwalk. For the past six months, Ojuromi has taken social media by storm, transforming the vibrant streets of Lagos into her personal runway, showcasing designs made from secondhand, thrifted clothes and scraps mostly sourced from local open-air hubs such as Yaba market. articles.title: Walk the talk: a week learning French with a personal prof in Normandy
articles.description: Hiring a personal tutor to learn French as we explore the beautiful city of Rouen proves a refreshing and affordable alternative to language school I’m walking beside the River Seine in the French city of Rouen when I realise that I’ve been speaking French – without pausing to find a word or struggle with grammar – for five whole minutes. Anna, my French “prof” for the week, nods encouragingly and so I continue. It’s a breakthrough moment, if only for my confidence. This is the last day of a DIY language course that I devised when Rouen’s language schools told me they were full for the only week I could get away. When I then enquired about their private tutors, I was told no one was available. This turned out to save me a pretty penny: language school tutors cost €60 an hour while Anna – who I discovered on the website Apprentus – is a cost-effective €19 an hour. Continue reading...

articles.title: The laundry miracle: how to solve 10 stubborn problems – from stains to rough towels to ‘permastank’
articles.description: For 1 million people on Reddit, the science of clothes-washing is a regular topic of discussion. I tried out their tips and discovered some simple, sustainable answers It started with a sunscreen stain – a yellowed collar on a white T-shirt that persisted wash after wash. A spray of stain remover did nothing; drying the shirt in the sun made it worse. An internet rabbit hole took me to the r/laundry subreddit , where I found my people: 995,000 of them, nerding out over the chemistry of clothes-washing. “People want to take better care of their stuff, but don’t have the knowledge,” says Eric Thompson, a former management consultant based near Seattle who moderates the forum under the name KismaiAesthetics. He took on the mantle after seeing someone suggest white vinegar to treat a burrito stain on an anorak. “If you pour vinegar on a burrito grease stain on white nylon, you now have orange nylon for eternity,” he says. “Acids bind colour to dye sites on nylon.” Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘We can’t be at the bottom indefinitely’: Can Britain’s most maligned service station be turned around?
articles.description: In 2022 and 2023, Hartshead Moor East, near Leeds, was voted the worst in Great Britain. Ever since, staff have been on a mission to redeem its reputation The crime issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to order In October 2023, at Skelton Lake service station on the M1 south-east of Leeds, Janine Gray received some bad news. She was surrounded by journalists and leading lights from the transport industry: people from the AA, the RAC, motorway service area chief executives, officials from National Highways. The big dogs. And it was among these gathered dignitaries that Gray heard the news she had been hoping, for the previous 12 months, not to hear. For the second year running, Hartshead Moor East – one half of the motorway services near Leeds that she managed – had been officially declared the worst service station in Britain. This poll, conducted annually by the consumer watchdog Transport Focus, always makes the news. It produces gags on Have I Got News For You, punning headlines in the papers, “and finally” segments on local TV channels. Now Gray and her staff would be subjected to another round of ridicule. Of all the country’s service stations, which have a s

articles.title: ‘I trusted a lot of people, and the wrong people, and I shouldn’t have’: Charlotte Kirk on navigating Hollywood
articles.description: The British actor took up writing and producing to have control over what she stars in after a scandal involving some of the most powerful men in the film business After a recent run as an assassin, a serial killer and a gangster, Charlotte Kirk was looking for something a little lighter, and surely nothing can be more jolly, more wholesome than a Christmas romcom. In Christmas & Chaos, Kirk plays Sadie, a pop star in search of a hit – or, to be more precise, three hits for a new musical by an impresario (a comedic Jason Isaacs who only appears on screen via video call). She has just a couple of weeks to come up with something with handsome-and-heartbroken composer (Ben McGregor). Kirk, who also produced the film, approached Jamie Adams, director of several low-budget British films, including Black Mountain Poets, intrigued by his regular use of improvisation. They worked out the story together, says Kirk, but made it without a script. All they knew was that “this was a Christmas movie, these two have got a deadline to make these hit songs and maybe there’ll be some kind of romance. And then it became something else, which is even more interesting.” Continue reading...

articles.title: You had me at LOL: some notes for the You’ve Got Mail reboot
articles.description: Substackers in love, dodgy romance scams and Jeff Bezos as the dashing lead … the film-makers behind the remake of the dial-up classic will be facing an embarrassment of pitches Assuming you have already heard about the You’ve Got Mail reboot, you are probably in one of two states. You are either excited that the news might be a signal of a long overdue romcom resurgence, or you are embittered because it’s another sign that Hollywood has run out of original ideas. I hold absolutely no truck with the latter view. Quite frankly, if there was ever a film in dire need of a reboot, then it’s You’ve Got Mail. The film is almost 28 years old, and it shows every single day of its age. You’ve seen it, you know how it goes. It’s about two people who use the futuristic new technology of email (email is no longer new) to communicate, despite being rival booksellers ( nobody reads books any more ), and eventually begin a relationship ( nobody wants to be in a relationship any more ). The whole thing is preposterous. Of course they should try again. Continue reading...

articles.title: South Park takes on the expensive, confusing world of club sports – with a nod to Heated Rivalry

The “blue wave” in the US midterms one week ago made it into the start of this week’s episode – but they are not discussed much more than that, because Donald Trump suffered a big defeat and “it’s no fun punching down on a helpless loser”. But it does mean the return of PC Principal, who delivers a funny torrent of profanities and belligerent vows of diversity and tolerance in a hyper-emboldened liberal version of the right-wing gloating we’ve seen in past elections. articles.description: Order a Diet Coke or invade Iran – that’s the choice facing the US president in one of several satirical games, as designers turn the gamification of politics back on the White House In early September, the Trump White House announced a surprising new addition to its official website. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. articles.title: Trump won't save Ukraine. But Marine Le Pen's betrayal could be worse | Mujtaba Rahman
articles.description: European leaders need urgently to prepare for a far-right French president who would cut off Kyiv’s financial lifeline Europe is consumed by two debates that matter less than it thinks, while neglecting one that matters enormously. The first is who should represent the EU in negotiations with Russia. This is largely irrelevant because there is little prospect of serious Ukraine peace talks before the end of winter - despite the fanfare that has surrounded discussions in Abu Dhabi this week. Russia has powerful incentives to escalate the war over the coming months in an attempt to break Ukraine’s economy and civilian morale. The second is Donald Trump’s approach to Ukraine. This matters less than it once did – and not only because he is now more constrained by a Democratic Congress. Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has provided no new US military aid to Kyiv. American weapons sales remain important to Ukraine’s war effort, but Trump’s military interventions in the Middle East have further strained supplies of the weapons Ukraine needs most – notably Patriot interceptors. articles.title: The Booker prize winner described a dystopian Britain. But haven’t we been living in that since Brexit? | Zoe Williams
articles.description: It didn’t need a novel: even Leave voters understand the damage that has been done, as does the PM. Now all he has to do is persuade his party Earlier this week, some people on the radio were talking about a very British dystopia. The government had disintegrated, but everyone was carrying on pretty much as they had before. Britain was isolated on the world stage and people missed Europe like hell, but weren’t allowed to visit, let alone live there. I thought the radio people were discussing Britain post-Brexit, circa 2022. In fact, they were talking about the plot of the Booker prize-winning novel The End of Everything . Its author, M John Harrison, is renowned now for being, at 81, the oldest winner of the award, as well as the first science fiction writer to win it. But let’s also carve out a space for him on the podium of dystopian fiction, as a writer who can describe an indeterminate future in terms that are both terrifying and sound like a couple of years ago. Zoe Williams is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: I’ve had a stinking cold this week – and I’m longing for good advice | Adrian Chiles
articles.description: Heavy and light colds tend to pass more quickly than middle-of-the-road ones. But should I stay in bed or continue mixing with others? How to define the cold that’s ruining your day? There’s a hierarchy. We start with the sniffle, the mere runny nose, scratchy throat or just feeling a little off. This is the slight cold. The nose becoming more blocked than runny, and a cough coming into play, entitles you to call it a heavy cold. Any of the aforementioned symptoms worsening, accompanied by hotness, shiveriness, aching and general misery, gives you the right to call it a stinking cold. There’s also a malady known as man-flu, but I have no truck with such a lazy, gender-specific categorisation. The only good thing about the stinking cold is that you have the green light to do sod all and repair to bed. This was me for three days this week, and it has firmed up a theory I have long held that you’re better off getting a stinker because it tends to come and go and be done with more quickly than the other varieties. This theory, I should point out, is based on my lived experience rather than any clinical expertise or any kind of research. Sorry – I felt too ill to bother with anything of

articles.title: Victorian Psycho review – Maika Monroe has a blast in unsteady horror romp
articles.description: The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel It’s not that hard to figure out why a lower-class woman toiling away in Victorian England would be so easily driven to violently murder everyone around her. If it’s not the brittle entitlement of those who employ you, it’s the unending misogyny of the system you’re forced to be a subservient part of, all the while being underpaid and undervalued and at the mercy of sexual violence, a multitude of diseases and an average lifespan of just 42. As Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) fills the frame in Victorian Psycho, heading to a new job as governess for a rich family, it’s easy to be on her side. Even as her murderous impulses start to rear their head, they’re made somewhat understandable, although Winifred isn’t just a woman reacting to the various injustices of the time – she’s one responding to a demon within her, a darkness she has chosen to embrace rather than resist. Darkness is her friend, a protection against harm, and a way to possess some sort of control in a world that has denied her any of it. Continue reading...

articles.title: Giulio Cesare in Egitto album review – Sabine Devieilhe’s exquisite Cleopatra could make stones weep
articles.description: Orliński/Devieilhe/Il Pomo d’Oro/Corti (Erato) Francesco Corti keeps the drama on the boil in this period instrument recording of Handel’s opera, with herculean feats of vocal dexterity by Jakub Józef Orliński in the title role – but it’s Sabine Devieilhe’s breathtaking queen who steals the show Giulio Cesare is Handel’s most popular opera with at least 15 versions in the current catalogue, several of them historical. This new recording by period instrument band Il Pomo d’Oro comes off the back of a European tour, thus benefiting from the experience of live performances. A lived-in quality is palpable here, from the frisson of emotional risk-taking to imaginatively decorated da capo sections. Leading from the keyboard, Francesco Corti keeps the drama on the boil, especially in recitatives where his resonant harpsichord sits comfortably in the mix. Timings are similar to Harry Bicket’s recent recording on Linn , but Corti invariably feels faster. Continue reading...

articles.title: Pierre Sage’s failure to fix defensive flaws leaves Crystal Palace seeking new solution
articles.description: A losing run, set-piece struggles and a call for help led Steve Parish to cut ties with the manager after five months The moment that summed up Crystal Palace’s season under Pierre Sage came five minutes before half-time at Selhurst Park on Sunday. After Palace had gone close to taking the lead on numerous occasions against Liverpool, the Frenchman must have feared the worst when Alexis Mac Allister headed in from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. The TV cameras immediately panned to Steve Parish in the stands. After the Palace chair removed his hands from in front of his eyes, his expression said everything you needed to know. The only surprise was that Sage had to wait until Thursday before his inevitable fate was confirmed . Not since the start of the 2017-18 season, after Frank de Boer was appointed as Palace’s first permanent foreign manager and sacked after five matches, have the club found themselves bottom. In their record 14th consecutive season in the top flight, and with preliminary work having started on building a new £200m main stand despite major doubts over funding, Palace cannot afford to be relegated. articles.description: Yttrium's 125-Fold Price Gap Looms Over Trump-Xi Talks In Shenzhen Authored by Michael Kern via OilPrice , China extended its pause on the October 2025 rare earth export controls to Jan. 10, but the April 2025 licensing rules that cover yttrium were never part of the pause. Argus prices yttrium about 125 times higher in Europe than in China, and Chinese customs data show yttrium oxide shipments to Japan fell to 4,000 kg in September from 51,000 kg a year earlier.  Non-Chinese yttrium is slow to arrive: Lynas isn’t due to start output until 2028, and USA Rare Earth has so far sent only demonstration-plant samples to one customer. China bought itself two more months this week by extending the pause on its sweeping October 2025 rare earth export controls to Jan. 10, Reuters reported , but the metal squeezing buyers hardest right now was never covered by it . That metal is yttrium, which sits under a separate set of licensing rules Beijing imposed in April 2025 on seven medium and heavy rare earths. articles.title: "Counted Every Single Bar": Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B In Physical Gold
articles.description: "Counted Every Single Bar": Tether Gold Gets Clean KPMG Audit Confirming $2.2B In Physical Gold Via Decrypt , Tether's gold-backed stablecoin, Tether Gold (XAUT), has completed its first full audit by KPMG, which found the token fully backed by physical gold , the company announced on Thursday. KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on the financial statements of TG Commodities, which issues XAUT, for the year ended December 31, 2025. An unqualified, or "clean," opinion means the auditor found that the statements fairly present the company's financial position, without reservations. Tether Gold (XAU₮) Becomes Tether's Second Stablecoin to Complete a Big Four Audit Learn more: https://t.co/eO0asUwvlI — Tether (@tether) November 12, 2026 As of the end of 2025, TG Commodities held 520,089.350 troy ounces of allocated gold, valued at $2.246 billion, against 520,089.300 XAUT tokens in issue , according to Tether. The gold is held in vaults in Switzerland, and each token represents an ownership interest in gold on specific bars. As part of the audit, KPMG physically counted and inspected every gold bar backing the token, rather than relying only on confirmations from custodians, Tether said.

articles.title: Yields Hit Session High After Ugly, Tailing 30Y Auction
articles.description: Yields Hit Session High After Ugly, Tailing 30Y Auction Amid the now daily firehose of news, the US Treasury managed to sneak in an auction of $25 billion in 30Y paper, and while not as ugly as Tuesday's terrible 10Y auction, today's auction was not pretty... at all. Stopping at a high yield of 5.441T%, the yield dipped from last month's 5.618% largely thanks to the uniform drop across the yield curve following the recent turmoil in the AI space (which means less competition for long end paper amid AI companies), but it tailed the 4.437% by 0.4bps, the biggest tail since June and the second highest since last November. The bid to cover was 2.401, down from 2.542 and the lowest since August and below the six auction average of 2.437%. Not terrible, not great.  The internals, likewise, could have been better: Indirects slid from 72.3% to 68.1%, which was also below the recent average of 70.5% (in fact the lowest since August too), but nowhere near as bad as the 10Y auction two days ago. And with Directs taking 20.5%, or about unchanged from last month's 20.9%, Dealers were left holding 11.4%, the highest since June. One option is a multistate compact. The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact commits member states to award their electoral votes to the presidential candidate who wins the most votes nationwide. It takes effect only when states holding at least 270 of the 538 electoral votes join. Eighteen states and the District of Columbia, together holding 222 electoral votes, have enacted it so far , according to National Popular Vote, the nonprofit group behind the compact. articles.title: Judge Denies Alaska Democratic US ​Senate Candidate's Request For Ballot Data
articles.description: Judge Denies Alaska Democratic US ​Senate Candidate's Request For Ballot Data Authored by Zachary Stieber via The Epoch Times, A judge on Nov. 11 denied a request from the Democrat running for a U.S. Senate seat representing Alaska. Alaska Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews turned down a lawsuit from Mary Peltola’s campaign that demanded immediate access to records identifying people whose absentee ballots the Alaska Division of Elections rejected , and the rationale for those rejections, including information potentially contained in a report provided to election observers. The two versions of that report are not public records and thus do not have to be disclosed to Peltola’s campaign, Matthews said in a 17-page decision. The documents contain confidential information and preliminary data, and observers are not allowed to retain copies, he said. Compelling the state to compile a report on reasons for the rejections is not reasonable, in part because the division is still processing ballots in the race for the seat, according to the ruling. The data could be gathered from a database but would need to be redacted first. “The Division is actively in the middle of counting ballots.

articles.title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?
articles.description: It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world? ‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms. One difference is immediately visible: this datacentre is made out of wood. Huge panels of cross-laminated timber arrived at the site pre-cut, and were assembled by crane according to instructions, like flatpack furniture. Aesthetically, this section of the datacentre is more like an Ikea before the fit-out, a cavernous, echoey, immaculately clean hangar. The wood is not EcoDataCenter’s only claim to sustainability; it is more than just cosmetic, says Wernvik, the company’s chief external relations and sustainability officer. “Compared with a traditional datacentre built with steel and concrete, we lower the embodied carbon of the full structure by three times.” With a complex the size of a football pitch,

articles.title: ‘Joni Mitchell sang Both Sides, Now over the phone to me’: folk music legend Judy Collins on her 87 remarkable years
articles.description: As she continues her farewell tour, the US singer-songwriter answers your questions on romance with Stephen Stills, friendship with Carly Simon and how folk underpins all pop How did you come into Joni Mitchell ’s orbit and how did you end up recording Both Sides, Now before she did? Steve-bayley I’m 48 years sober, but in the old days I drank. One night in 1967, I was passed out and the phone rang at about 3am. It was my friend [the musician, songwriter and producer] Al Kooper. He said he’d been at a club and had run into this woman, Joni, who wrote songs. He put her on the phone and she sang Both Sides, Now over the phone. It was brilliant. I said: “I’ll be right over.” I recorded it the next day and it became a huge hit. I don’t think Joni was too happy that I was the first to record it, but she was very generous and I’ve since recorded many of her songs. She was unknown then, so I’m proud that I was able to help introduce her to the world. She’s one of the great writers of all time. Continue reading...

articles.title: Rats, dengue and an all-day stench: can Panama City solve its waste crisis?
articles.description: For decades, mountains of waste have blighted poor neighbourhoods on the edge of the city. But as the problems spread, a belated reckoning is under way Life in San Miguelito has long been dictated by rubbish. Routes to the shop are carefully navigated to avoid pungent mountains of rotting waste, some visible from space. Driving during the rainy season is a perilous obstacle course, dodging black bin bags and rusty fridges in the middle of the road. Children are taught early to avoid the river, the rubbish, the rats, yet mosquito-borne diseases still stalk the community. For Yamileth, who lives with her family on one of the steep, narrow streets that thread the hillside neighbourhood, the waste is a constant backdrop to daily life. Mornings are punctuated by the stench and buzz of flies, and in the evenings you can hear rats scuttling and stray dogs rustling as they rip open bags in search of food among the rubbish heaps, known in slang as patacones (also the name of a staple side dish made from green plantains). articles.title: Spare a thought for poor Nige, clearly missing his podcast chats with Russell Brand
articles.description: It’s not been a good week for Farage. Aside from that interview and disrespect from the BBC, he’s lost another senior Reform official It’s a day late, but please observe a two-minute silence for Nigel Farage. Lest we forget. Sad to say, but Nige just hasn’t been quite the same since Sunday’s Remembrance service at the Cenotaph. Like me, you might have thought that he had been in Whitehall to honour those who had died in two world wars and subsequent armed conflicts. Only it turns out he was really there to commemorate himself. Through his personal valet, Richard Tice, Nige has let it be known that he was extremely angry with the BBC’s coverage of the service. The cameras had spent too long lingering on the faces of the king, other members of the royal family and prime ministers past and present. When what they should have been focused on throughout was Nige. He was the one we were all there to see. The man who had done more for his country than anyone else. To have disrespected him in this way was unforgivable. Let’s hope the BBC has got its act together by next year. Continue reading...

articles.description: A speech by the leader of the opposition exemplifies much that is wrong with the way British politics conventionally talks about benefit claimants There is a big difference between expenditure that is rising and a rise that is “out of control”. The amount Britain spends on social security is in the former category. Too much political rhetoric around the subject assumes that it is in the latter one. The Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts the growth in welfare spending over the next five years at 0.2%-0.5% of gross domestic product, from £353bn this year to £431bn in 2032. That money might well be suboptimally deployed. There are rival demands on the state’s resources and a reasonable debate to be had about priorities at the Department for Work and Pensions. articles.description: One reader sounds a warning about all our devices that are connected to the internet, following a series of cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges Well done to Alex Pearce for unplugging his fridge from the internet ( Hot fridges, a fake nuclear alert and a $6bn heist: are we in the foothills of a hacking epidemic?, 8 November ). My only question is why he didn’t do it a few weeks earlier, when the first round of hacked fridges were headline news for several days. Your article notes that there are millions of devices connected to the internet. This sea of domestic and industrial controllers, known as the “internet of things” in marketing literature and the “internet of shit” by engineers, all have several things in common: their firmware is almost never upgraded, software security features are a fig leaf and the vast majority can run without an internet connection. articles.title: Clearing up confusion over iodine in milk | Letters
articles.description: Cow’s milk is not a natural source of iodine. It is fortified, at the cow, notes Dale Vince of the Green Britain Foundation You report that scientists say moving even partly from dairy products to vegan alternatives could lead to deficiencies in iodine and other micronutrients if the substitutes are not fortified ( Swapping from dairy to plant-based milk, cheese and yoghurt ‘could lead to micronutrient deficiencies’, 4 November ). To be clear, cow’s milk is not a natural source of iodine. It is fortified, at the cow. As the paper published in the Lancet Planetary Health explains, iodine is in milk because it is added to cattle feed. The vitamin B12 is there because cobalt is added to the feed so the cow’s gut bacteria can make it. Britain has been doing this for decades. If fortification is the answer, and the paper’s authors say it is, then fortify plant milk. It’s better for us and the planet than cow’s milk. Continue reading...

articles.description: A reader highlights how the government’s immigration changes are affecting those who have been granted asylum and wish to apply for indefinite leave to remain I am writing as a refugee who has lived in the UK since 2007. I claimed asylum in 2007, and my appeal was allowed by the first-tier tribunal (immigration and asylum) in February 2020. However, because of Home Office delays, I did not receive my five-year refugee permission until June 2022. I applied for indefinite leave to remain in June 2025, but my application was refused because I had not completed five years from the date my refugee permission was granted. I was therefore expecting to apply again in June 2027. Continue reading...

articles.description: Creation of Sport Org sparks disquiet at governing bodies Smaller sports concerned they might be taken over The leaders of Britain’s Olympic and Paralympic sports have been responsible for some of the country’s greatest successes over the past two decades. But there are changes afoot that are increasingly ruffling feathers and stoking fears. Most people will not have heard of Sport Org, the organisation recently set up by UK Sport. Essentially, it evolved out of British Curling, and now uses its leaders and expertise across curling, para-curling, para table tennis, squash and, from 2030, bobsleigh and skeleton. articles.title: Chicken curry and potato croquettes: Ranie Saidi’s recipes for a Malaysian feast
articles.description: Leeks play a major part in two Malaysian-inspired dishes: they melt into coconut in a marvellous chicken curry, and pair perfectly with peas in crunchy potato croquettes Since moving from Malaysia to London more than a decade ago, I’ve slowly brought leeks into my everyday cooking. Their gentle sweetness reminds me of banana shallots, and I love how they melt into this chicken gulai . Bergedil ( or begedil or perkedel) have always been one of my favourite street-food snacks, and are found at stalls across Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia. In Malay cooking, they’re often made using mashed potato that’s mixed with minced meat, shaped and fried, but my version uses leeks, frozen peas and leftover herbs, plus an orange, chilli and yoghurt dip. articles.title: ‘Maga is dead, Maga is effeminate’: why has the manosphere rejected Trump?
articles.description: As public mood has shifted on Israel-Gaza and the Iran war, so has the manosphere’s devotion to the US president Earlier this week, Donald Trump announced that the UFC president, Dana White, was to become his press secretary. The US president hoped the creator of Power Slap, a face-slapping league which one of the world’s leading neurologists called “a sport inconsistent with the intelligence of humans”, might be the right man to deliver his daily rebuttals to the media. Trump later backtracked on the appointment, saying he was “only kidding” , yet it is easy to understand why he might be pining for White’s muscles, trash talk and thirst for athletic violence. White is representative of the way Trump transcended politics in 2024 to become a celebrated figure in the manosphere, the loosely defined cluster of male content creators who have a direct line to America’s bored and aggrieved young men. On the night of the 2024 election, White stood at the victory podium reading out “thank yous” to the formerly heterodox podcast bros who came out for Trump: “the Nelk Boys, Adin Ross, Theo Von, Bussin’ With The Boys, and last but not least, the mighty and powerful Joe Rogan”. articles.title: Time for a harsh truth: even with Netanyahu gone, the killing won’t stop in Gaza | Owen Jones
articles.description: It’s naive to think the Israeli opposition will act very differently. Look at what it has said about even the most vulnerable Palestinians “Every child, every baby in Gaza is the enemy.” In a normal society, a politician who said something so depraved would face total reputational ruin. Not so in Israel. Meet Moshe Feiglin, previously considered a “far-right outcast”, who has just been elected to Israel’s legislature. He said this last May , but he has also called for more Palestinian babies to die and for Gaza’s entire population, newborns included , to be expelled. In last month’s election, Feiglin formed an alliance with Bezalel Smotrich, the far-right finance minister. Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed this “important union” and praised their “national responsibility”. Feiglin’s words are not simply the ravings of an extremist politician. Israel has waged what Save the Children describes as a “ war on children ”. A UN independent commission concluded earlier this year that Israeli forces had deliberately targeted and killed Palestinian children. articles.title: Thanks to American oligarchy, Jensen Huang’s midlife crisis is a problem for all of us | Moira Donegan
articles.description: At a time when individual men wield massive power, the ramifications of the Nvidia CEO’s affair could be enormous One of the reasons you want to distribute power and responsibility in powerful organizations and high-stakes enterprises is so that the narcissism or myopia of one man do not come to carry outsized consequences. When power is spread out across multiple people, it matters less if one of those people is prone to flattery, or in the midst of a midlife crisis, or perhaps just a bit stupid; the limits on his power become limits on the fallout of his character flaws. articles.title: Barcelona v Arsenal: Women’s Champions League – live
articles.description: ⚽️ WCL updates from 5.45pm GMT kick-off ⚽️ Live scoreboard | And email Simon Renée Slegers has a bit of a chat about the game, and about how injuries are impacting Arsenal’s squad: We have an incredible squad, we have a lot of depth in the squad. It’s always going to happen that you have absences. Of course we’re missing those players but we always have players who can step up. We need everyone, so the squad is ready for tonight. It’s a maze around the Camp Nou building site, and finding the media entrance involved a lot of confused stewards and different directions. We’re in though, and what a stadium it’s going to be when the work is done. It’s really hard to know how Arsenal will fare here. They could snatch a cheeky 1-0 win or lose by five, and neither would be that much of a surprise. It’s great to see Frida Maanum in the 10 and Alessia Russo in the centre-forward position. articles.description: Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013 For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking , consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one. The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. articles.description: Left out of squad to tour South Africa, spin bowler’s exclusion points to a sport reshaped by the needs of T20 and hard data During the summer, Sky Sports would frequently run an advert for one of English cricket’s blue-chip financial sponsors. I forget its exact name – something like WXYZ Tradify or Crypto Max 301 or Wealth Centaur would be my guess. But I remember there was a mind-shreddingly banal male voiceover (“diversify your forex contingents and start making your money bleed today”), to which England players like Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell were depicted engaging in various feats of staged cricketing heroism. Right up until the moment Shoaib Bashir steps up to bowl. Bashir delivers his trademark off-break with that famously high release point. Upon which Bethell steps down the track and smashes the Wealth Centaur-branded ball back past his face, smashing a hole in the CGI wall and sending it into a hail of digital rain. Poor Shoaib. A passenger in the Ashes, sidelined for most of the home Test series, and now even getting clouted in the ad breaks. And in retrospect that was the point when we should all have realised that one English cricket’s weirder recent Test careers w

Launched in July 2023, the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission promised to create the largest cosmic map ever made, encompassing a third of the sky and more than 10bn years of cosmic history. articles.title: War Requiem review – in the cathedral where it premiered, Britten’s masterpiece has lost none of its power
articles.description: Coventry Cathedral Kazuki Yamada led the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra and chorus and soloists Christian Gerhaher, Andrew Staples and Olga Peretyatko in this monumental and moving performance of Britten’s towering work The premiere of Britten’s War Requiem as part of the consecration of Coventry’s new cathedral in 1962 left its German baritone soloist Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau “completely undone”. Sculptor Barbara Hepworth listened on the radio and declared herself “profoundly moved”. The composer described it as a “call for peace”; critics unanimously reached for the word “masterpiece”. More than half a century later, some of the boy choristers from that world premiere were in attendance as the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra returned to Coventry Cathedral to perform the War Requiem – now marking both Armistice Day and 50 years since Britten’s own death. The work has lost none of its currency. Wilfred Owen ’s texts still shock, the most explosive passages of Britten’s score continue to detonate as if physically threatening. And the mass cooperation of so many musicians continues to represent Britten’s hopefulness in humanity like nothing else. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I railed against the stereotype of the humourless lesbian’: the cheeky, feminist photography of Jill Posener
articles.description: Her witty photos served as a rebuttal to 80s misogyny and Thatcherite conservatism. Now 50 years on, the photographer is receiving an overdue retrospective. ‘I loved that we could respond with humour,’ she says. If it were a lady it would get its bottom pinched. If this lady was a car she’d run you down.” These are the words that Jill Posener immortalised in November 1979, when she picked her way through traffic on London’s Farringdon Road to photograph something most would have overlooked: a graffitied billboard. The first sentence was there by design – a sexist attempt at wit intended to promote a new Fiat. The second she has since been repeatedly accused of adding herself. In reality, the image-maker, playwright and nonprofit founder explains from her home in California, the now infamous phrase had been daubed by two women working at the nearby offices of the socialist newspaper Morning Star. “They had seen the billboard go up and were so incensed that they came up with this solution,” Posener recalls. “They didn’t think anything of it until they saw the postcard. I sent them a whole bunch and we all had a good laugh.” Continue reading...
